authority_basis: ONE shared, scenario-agnostic memory/reactivation policy drives the entire G4 scenario family (S10-S13). Rules inspect ONLY generic memory dimensions: lifecycle state, memory tier, reopen-condition state, blocker state, evidence freshness, task relevance, dependency centrality, authority status, current epoch, retrieval/context budget. No scenario id, no knowledge literals, no expected outcomes. Dispositions are test-only: reopening means ELIGIBLE FOR RENEWED EVALUATION, never promotion; memory never changes authority, never makes negative knowledge permanent, never promotes CANDIDATE directly to ACTIVE, never rewrites sealed epochs. PROVISIONAL_SCENARIO_TEST_POLICY — never constitutional truth.

rules.rationale: PERMANENT_BY_OPERATOR_AUTHORITY records cannot auto-reopen on ordinary reopen evidence; operator revocation semantics are unspecified and the ambiguity stays explicit
a satisfied machine-readable reopen condition makes the record eligible for renewed evaluation via the governed M4 path — NOT promotion (DORMANT->ACTIVE stays forbidden)
condition semantics unknown => fail closed, no reopen
unsatisfied reopen condition leaves the record dormant/suppressed
high task relevance keeps the object in default active context; this is task need, not institutional age
a dormant object whose reopen condition fires is retrieved into context for renewed evaluation (never automatically promoted)
irrelevant-to-task historical objects move out of default active context without erasing history
operator-permanent negative knowledge stays suppressed pending operator review; ordinary reopen evidence cannot stop suppression
reopen condition fires for the exact governed scope: suppression ceases, the negative-knowledge record is retained
unsatisfied/unknown reopen condition: suppression continues; the record is never deleted
